candidates.text:
The biggest engineering mistake I made at Figure was building a tendon-based hand

Our first hand design in 2022 was a tendon hand for our F.01 robot. At a high level, the tendon approach sounds appealing, which is why I chose it: you get more space for packaging actuators since the forearm is larger, potentially higher degrees of freedom, and it's biologically inspired

We built and manufactured this entire hand and tested it in early 2023. If you saw it in person, it was truly an engineering work of art. It turned out to be one of the worst engineering decisions I've made, maybe the worst in four years. Tendons are a complete local maximum, and that only becomes clear in hindsight, after exploring every other possible hand design. Figure is unique in that we've now built and tested several hand architectures, which gave us a clear sense of where to head

Figure is working on our next generation hand, and it's so much better than anything you can do with tendons, it's not even funny

candidates.text:
You’ve read the books.

You’ve bookmarked the threads.

You’ve watched the podcasts, bought the courses, studied the frameworks, saved the quotes, written the goals.

You KNOW more than enough.

And yet…

Your life still looks DANGEROUSLY similar to how it looked last year.

Same ideas sitting untouched.

Same opportunities passing by.

Same promises that THIS TIME you’re finally going to do it.

Still waiting for the lucky break.

Still waiting for everything to “click.”

Still waiting to become the person you already KNOW you could be.

So let’s cut the bullshit.

YOU DO NOT HAVE AN INFORMATION PROBLEM.

You cannot read your way out of this.

Another podcast won’t save you.

Another productivity system won’t save you.

Another morning routine, ice bath, habit tracker, journal, or copy of Atomic Habits won’t save you.

Because you’ve spent YEARS trying to solve a SUBCONSCIOUS PROBLEM with CONSCIOUS INFORMATION.

Imagine running a marathon with three enormous hurdles planted across the track.

You’re strong enough to finish.

You’re fast enough to WIN.

But you keep staring at the horizon.

So every time you reach one of those hurdles…

BANG.

Face-first into the ground.

You get back up.

Run harder.

BANG.

Fall again.

And eventually, after eating dirt enough times, you start wondering whether there’s something wrong with you.

There isn’t.

YOU JUST HAVEN’T TRAINED YOURSELF TO CLEAR THE FUCKING HURDLES.

And there are 3 of them.

HURDLE #1: SELF-DOUBT

You see what you should do.
You FEEL the impulse.
You’re almost ready to move.
Then the voice arrives:
“What if this doesn’t work?”
“What if I can’t pull it off?”
“What if I’m wrong?”
That tiny hesitation is enough.
The window CLOSES.
The moment DIES.
Another opportunity gets BURIED.

HURDLE #2: DAYDREAMING

You’re so busy thinking about the life you want that you miss the pieces of it already sitting RIGHT IN FRONT OF YOU.
The person you should call.
The idea you should pursue.
The opening nobody else noticed.
The resource you forgot you had.
The move staring you directly in the face.
You could be sitting on a GOLD MINE while fantasising about finding gold.
And that is exactly how people spend YEARS waiting for opportunities they’ve ALREADY been given.

HURDLE #3: THE STORY

This one is especially vicious.
Because after you fail to move, your mind has to give you a reason WHY.
So it manufactures a story.
“The timing isn’t right.”
“I’ll wait until payday.”
“I need to research it more.”
“I’ll come back to this.”
“I’ll start Monday.”
And because the story comes from inside your own head…
you believe it.
Again.
And again.
And AGAIN.
Until weeks become months.
Months become years.
And suddenly you realise you’ve spent a terrifying amount of your LIFE preparing to become someone you could have started becoming YEARS AGO.

Some people eventually mistake these patterns for their personality.
They say:
“That’s just how I am.”

Fuck that.

A hurdle is NOT an identity.

A hurdle is something you LEARN TO CLEAR.

And once you can SEE the hurdles…

You can train yourself to LEAP over them.

Because nobody wins a race by stopping in front of every hurdle and intellectually analysing it.

You train the RESPONSE.

You see the hurdle.

You JUMP.

You see another.

You JUMP.

Until the thing that used to STOP you becomes something you instinctively CLEAR.

THAT is exactly what the latest RubiPill release was built to train.

OPPORTUNITY PILL

Trains your mind to SEARCH.
To notice openings.
To recognise leverage.
To see resources, connections and possibilities hiding in plain sight.

To develop an OPPORTUNITY CONSCIOUSNESS that automatically searches your environment asking:
“WHAT CAN I DO WITH THIS?”

Because opportunity is EVERYWHERE.

The question is whether your mind has been trained to SEE it.

CARPE DIEM PILL

This is the AXE.
It trains a bias toward ACTION.
See it.
Choose.
MOVE.
Instead of watching another opportunity disappear while you THINK about it…
YOU SEIZE IT.

"Not to be an annoying VC, but Jevons Paradox is a freaking wonderful thing."

"Because what's happening is — I see the data on all this stuff. Our companies, we see the gross margins going up. At the same time as AI usage is going way up, their gross margins are also going up. Because they are the beneficiaries of intelligence getting cheaper and cheaper to meter."

"On the other hand — and I see this from the model companies we work with — their cohorts are getting better and better and better."

"So it's not like they're facing price competition, and their businesses are going into the gutter. They have phenomenal businesses, where because they're able to provide intelligence at increasingly cheap prices, their businesses actually get better and better."

"So I actually think this is an 'everybody wins' situation."

candidates.text:
Canva just cut its 2026 growth forecast by a third, from 30% to 20%, and blamed the cost of serving AI features to a prosumer base. 

That number reopened the question hanging over every pre-AI software company: is AI a feature you add, or the thing that ends you? 

This week @HarryStebbings, @rodriscoll and I worked through that, plus Jeff Dean and Demis Hassabis leaving Google, Elon's $16.8B first installment on Terrafab, Revolut's reported $50B CEO package, and Whatnot raising at a $20B valuation.

What we covered:

- Why Canva is probably worth ~$12B today, and why Rory thinks that's the existential discount rather than the growth math
- The scarier version of churn: our agents at SaaStr built our entire ad creative stack and never once considered using Canva
- Why companies that hesitated in 2023 and 2024 are paying for it in 2026 and 2027, with Palantir and Replit as the counterexamples
- Jeff Dean's exit as a compute allocation story, not a comp story
- The third compensation band that now exists, and what god-tier packages do to the rest of the team
- Why every company in my portfolio not run by a founder is going to zero
- The real threat to HubSpot, which isn't anyone vibe coding their own CRM
- Plus 3 quotable moments each from Harry, Rory and me
